identity.name: EURO PRATIK SALES LIMITED
identity.industry: Interior Surfaces / Decorative Wall Panels & Laminates

summary.oneLiner: Euro Pratik delivered robust margin expansion (43.1% EBITDA) despite a 7% top-line miss caused by temporary North India construction bans, with management guiding for a ~25% rebound in Q4FY26 driven by pent-up demand and consolidation of the URO Veneer acquisition. The asset-light, fast-fashion model continues to drive superior profitability compared to manufacturing peers, while strategic acquisitions deepen B2C retail penetration.

one-line thesis: Euro Pratik delivered robust margin expansion (43.1% EBITDA) despite a 7% top-line miss caused by temporary North India construction bans, with management guiding for a ~25% rebound in Q4FY26 driven by pent-up demand and consolidation of the URO Veneer acquisition. The asset-light, fast-fashion model continues to drive superior profitability compared to manufacturing peers, while strategic acquisitions deepen B2C retail penetration.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 80.4 Cr (+7% YoY, impacted by North India ban); EBITDA: INR 34.6 Cr (+26% YoY), Margin: 43.1% (+600 bps YoY); PAT: INR 23.6 Cr (+17% YoY), Margin: 29.4%; Order Book: Not disclosed (B2B/B2C inventory model); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, asset-light model implies low capex intensity. One-offs: Q1 FY26 fire loss mentioned as past event; Q3 revenue suppressed by GRAP-4 construction restrictions in North India (est. 8-10% sales impact).
guidance: Q4FY26 Revenue Growth: ~25% YoY (consolidated, including M&A); Margins: Sustained ~40% +/- 2-3%; Order Inflow: Expected recovery in North India post-ban lift; Capex: Limited to working capital and minor warehouse expansion (80% utilized).
order book & pipeline: N/A - Company operates on a fast-fashion inventory model with 3,000+ SKUs rather than a project-based order book; distribution network spans 188 distributors across 138 cities.
segment / subsidiary detail: Decorative Wall Panels: 66.5% of 9M revenue; Decorative Laminates: 26.9% of 9M revenue; Allied Products (films, adhesives): Remainder. Wall panels and laminates growing consistently; premium laminates complement panel sales.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Tier-II/III cities (targeting 12-15% annual distributor growth); New product launches (1,000+ designs/year); Forward integration via acquisitions (URO Veneer, Hues Ply Decor JV) to capture B2C retail margins; International expansion (US, UAE).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margins expanded to 43.1% in Q3 (vs ~36-37% historically) due to operating leverage and high-margin innovative products; management targets sustainable 40% +/- 2-3% range. Asset-light model (36+ contract manufacturers) keeps fixed costs low.
capex / expansion: Minimal capex required due to asset-light manufacturing model; warehouse capacity currently at 80% utilization across 1.84 lakh sq. ft.; potential INR 2 Cr investment planned for Hues Ply Decor JV in Q1 FY27.
capital allocation: Focus on M&A for forward integration (retail chains, premium brands) and working capital for inventory expansion; no dividend policy explicitly detailed in call, prioritizing reinvestment for growth.
risks & watch-items: Regulatory restrictions on construction (e.g., pollution bans in North India); Dependency on contract manufacturers for quality consistency (mitigated by 10-person KMP team); Competition from fragmented unorganized players; Raw material price volatility (passed through via pricing).
management quality / tone: Confident and bottom-line focused; acknowledged temporary top-line headwinds from external factors (pollution ban) but emphasized strong recovery trajectory; transparent about M&A strategy and integration synergies.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'miss' in Q3 revenue (7% vs industry 18-20%) is entirely attributed to a temporary regulatory ban in North India (22.4% of sales mix), with management indicating an 8-10% absolute sales deferral to Q4, implying underlying organic growth was likely ~15-17%. The acquisition of URO Veneer creates a unique B2B2C flywheel where Euro Pratik sources products for URO's retail platform, booking organic growth through a consolidated entity while eliminating inter-company sales.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Construction bans in North India temporarily suppressed demand for interior finishes. | Dhabriya Polywood | beneficiary | Low | Competitor in PVC profiles; may have seen relative resilience if product mix differed, but sector-wide headwind likely affected all. |
| Shift towards organized players and premium aesthetic solutions benefits asset-light innovators. | Greenpanel Industries | beneficiary | Med | Peer in wood composite/interior segment; benefits from same structural shift to organized interior solutions though product mix differs. |

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims *15.87% market share as "Leader in Organized Decorative Wall Panels Industry"; the deck's own footnote qualifies this as "by revenue in the organized Decorative Wall Panels industry in Fiscal 2023" (source: Technopak Report), i.e. a Fiscal 2023 measure, not a current one.
- Dual premium brand strategy — "Euro Pratik and Gloirio" described as "Premium brands targeting upper-middle and luxury segments", run with "Independent distributor networks, dedicated warehouses, unique design philosophies, and separate leadership teams and channel partners".
- Positions itself as providing "high-quality, eco-friendly alternatives to traditional wall décor products like wallpaper, wood, and paint", operating "as a leading seller and marketer in the decorative wall panel and laminate industry" — a seller/marketer, not a manufacturer.
- Distribution moat: "Distribution network in 148 cities & 205 Distributors (203 in India and 2 outside India) across 25 States & 6 Union Territories", with sales contribution "From India: 99.11%, Outside India: 0.89%".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition — Uro Veneer World] Forward integration into South India retail: "One of South India's most trusted interior décor brands", with 90 professionals, 3,500+ interior designers partnered, 125+ categories, 18,000+ SKUs, 1,50,000+ satisfied customers, 2,800+ contractors and OEMs served, and 200+ daily visitors. Deck states "Revenue: ₹ 49.7 crs with PAT: ₹ 6.5 crs in H1FY26" and "Projected Revenue: ₹ ~115 crs with Projected PAT: ₹ ~20 crs in FY 27".
- [Acquisition — Chawla Brothers] North India expansion: established 1978, "a legacy business in plywood and decorative surfaces", with 450+ dealer network, 7,500 sq.ft showrooms/experience centres, 40-50 visitors/day footfall, 51,000 sq. ft. warehousing, locations at Jalandhar and Ludhiana, territory served "Punjab, Haryana, Jammu & Parts of Himachal Pradesh", and "Projected Revenue: ₹ ~80 crs in FY27".
- [Listing] "Successfully listed on the NSE & BSE" is shown as a 2026 milestone; Scrip Code 544519 (BSE) and symbol EUROPRATIK (NSE).
- [Industry sizing — Technopak] Indian Wall Panel Market ₹2,418 Cr (FY24) → ₹2,841 Cr (FY25) → ₹5,507 Cr (FY29E), with "The organised market is expected to reach 75% by FY2029"; Indian Wall Decorative Market ₹34,273 Cr (FY24) → ₹36,622 Cr (FY25) → ₹62,890 Cr (FY29E).
- [Prior acquisitions] Earlier bolt-ons named with their stated rationale: Vougue Decor (consolidates the "Gloirio" brand), Euro Pratik Laminate LLP / Lamage Decor (adds Lamage Decor portfolio), Millenium Decor (increases scale in interior wall cladding), EuroPratik Intex LLP (expands into interior and exterior surfaces) and Euro Pratik USA, LLC (direct U.S. presence).
